objective.text: Handle invalid stored values when hydrating a backed-enum cast.

difficulty.rationale: Locate the invalid-data failure at cast access rather than silently coercing a case.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

files.source:
<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

enum Status: string
{
    case Active = 'active';
    case Paused = 'paused';
}

class Service extends Model
{
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['status' => Status::class];
    }
}

$service = (new Service())->newFromBuilder(['id' => 1, 'status' => 'retired']);

echo $service->status->value;

stem: The database row contains status="retired", which is not an enum case. What happens at the final line?

options.text: active is printed because the first case is a default.
options.rationale: The cast has no first-case fallback for an unknown stored value.
options.misconception: The cast has no first-case fallback for an unknown stored value.

options.text: An empty string is printed because invalid values always cast to null.
options.rationale: A non-null invalid enum value does not receive null fallback semantics.
options.misconception: A non-null invalid enum value does not receive null fallback semantics.

options.text: retired is printed as an automatically added enum case.
options.rationale: Backed enums have a closed set of cases; hydration does not add new cases.
options.misconception: Backed enums have a closed set of cases; hydration does not add new cases.

options.text: A ValueError is thrown when the invalid value is converted to the enum.
options.rationale: The backed-enum cast uses the declared cases; it cannot turn retired into a valid Status.
